newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says German could meet EMU targets.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says German could meet EMU targets.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that Germany still had a chance to meet the fiscal criteria needed to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Speaking to reporters on the way into a meeting of parliament's finance committee, he said: "We have the possibilty to meet the criteria. It all depends on growth."
The Maastricht treaty sets a range of economic targets to qualify for EMU including limiting budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product and public debt to 60 percent.
Waigel said the criteria should be "stringently applied", adding "3.0 is 3.0", a reference meant to dispel speculation that the deficit criterion could be interpreted loosely.
